title: Pricing coefficient and selling price
summary: The theoretical price of each product: cost × coefficient, plus taxes and fees.

what: The selling price has to cover the raw materials, every other cost of the business and the profit you want. The handbook treats the desired profit as one more cost, and sets it before deciding to open.

The method uses a coefficient: it multiplies each product's standard cost (from its recipe card) and then adds taxes and fees on sales. The result is a theoretical price you must compare with the competition and adjust with commercial judgment.
formula: Non-raw-material costs = salaries + payroll charges + rent + utilities + general expenses + amortization
Desired net profit = investment × annual return % ÷ 12 + monthly draw
Coefficient = 1 + (non-raw-material costs + profit before tax) ÷ COGS
Net price = standard unit cost × coefficient
Menu price = net price × (1 + VAT + gross income tax + cards + health & safety)

variables.name: Costs not related to raw materials
variables.description: Staff (with payroll charges), rent, utilities, general expenses and amortization of the investment.

variables.name: Desired profit
variables.description: The return you expect on your investment plus what you want to draw for your work, before income tax.

variables.name: COGS
variables.description: Cost of goods consumed in the month.

variables.name: Standard unit cost
variables.description: The raw material cost of a product, from its recipe card.

steps: Add up the costs that aren't raw materials.
Set the desired net profit and convert it to profit before tax.
Work out the cost of goods consumed in the month.
Multiply each product's standard cost by the coefficient.
Add taxes and fees on sales to get the menu price.

examples.title: Handbook coefficient
paragraphs: Non-raw-material costs: salaries $57,000 + payroll charges (48%) $27,360 + rent $41,000 + utilities $13,000 + general expenses $90,000 + amortization ($3,000,000 ÷ 36) $83,333.33 = $311,693.33.

examples.title: Bakery prices
paragraphs: With 21% VAT, 3% gross income tax and 0.5% health & safety levy (24.5%): croissants $34.74 × 1.245 = $43.25.
Adding the 5% card fee (29.5% in total): $34.74 × 1.295 = $44.99.

notes.text: The handbook says "24.5% (21% VAT, 3% gross income tax, 5% cards and 0.5% health & safety)" and uses 1.245, but those four components add up to 29.5%: 24.5% is the total without cards. That's why you see the breakdown here and choose whether you accept cards.
The handbook shows $43.27 for the croissants; multiplying without rounding intermediate values gives $43.25.
The course spreadsheet uses 50% payroll charges; we follow the handbook, which uses 48%.
Don't price with the "rule of 3" or just by looking at the competition: combine the cost study, competitors' prices and your commercial judgment.
If your price is well below the market, you can raise it; if it's well above, review the product or take it off the menu.
As a reasonable minimum return, the handbook suggests twice the yield of a three-year government bond.

unit-cost.label: Standard unit cost
unit-cost.placeholder: Raw material cost of the product from its recipe card (e.g. 12)

salaries.label: Salaries (month)
salaries.placeholder: Total staff salaries, including the owner's if they work there (e.g. 57000)

services.label: Utilities (month)
services.placeholder: Electricity, gas, water, internet and other utilities (e.g. 13000)

general-expenses.label: General expenses (month)
general-expenses.placeholder: Cleaning, laundry, stationery, professional fees, etc. (e.g. 90000)

investment.label: Investment
investment.placeholder: Total invested to open the business (e.g. 3000000)

amortization-months.label: Amortization period
amortization-months.placeholder: Months over which the investment is written off (e.g. 36)
amortization-months.hint: The handbook assumes equipment is worth nothing after 3 years.

annual-return-rate.label: Expected annual return on investment
annual-return-rate.placeholder: Annual percentage you want to earn as an investor (e.g. 32)
annual-return-rate.hint: At least twice what a government bond yields.

monthly-withdrawal.label: Owner's monthly draw
monthly-withdrawal.placeholder: What you want to take home monthly for your work, net (e.g. 50000)

include-card-fee.label: Do you accept cards?
include-card-fee.placeholder: Add the card processing fee to the price

card-fee-rate.label: Card processing fee
card-fee-rate.placeholder: Percentage charged by the card issuer (e.g. 5)

outputs.non-raw-material-costs: Costs not related to raw materials
outputs.sales-tax-rate: Taxes and fees on the price

steps.non-raw-material-costs: Non-raw-material costs = salaries + charges + rent + utilities + general expenses + amortization = {salaries} + {socialCharges} + {rent} + {services} + {generalExpenses} + {amortization} = {nonRawMaterialCosts}
steps.net-profit: Desired net profit = monthly return + draw = {monthlyReturn} + {monthlyWithdrawal} = {netProfit}
steps.coefficient: Coefficient = 1 + (non-raw-material costs + profit before tax) ÷ COGS = 1 + ({nonRawMaterialCosts} + {grossProfit}) ÷ {costOfGoodsConsumed} = {coefficient}
steps.sales-tax-rate: Taxes and fees = VAT + gross income tax + cards + health & safety = {vatRate} + {grossIncomeTaxRate} + {cardFeeRate} + {safetyHygieneRate} = {salesTaxRate}
